findings.claim: a rebuilt title typically reduces resale value by 20% to 40%
findings.correctedValue: Keep 20% to 40%, attributed to Kelley Blue Book as an 'industry rule of thumb'. KBB applies it to any 'salvaged, reconstructed or otherwise clouded' title (not rebuilt only) and says such vehicles should be appraised case by case. Suggested: 'Kelley Blue Book's rule of thumb is that a salvage or rebuilt title cuts a vehicle's value by 20% to 40%.' Do not add the 65-75% unrepaired-salvage figure seen on secondary sites (no primary source found).
findings.quote: A salvaged, reconstructed or otherwise 'clouded' title has a permanent negative effect on the value of a vehicle. The industry rule of thumb is to deduct 20% to 40% of the Blue Book® Value, but salvage title vehicles really should be privately appraised on a case-by-case basis in order to determine their market value.
findings.verified_how: WebFetch of kbb.com FAQ page, 2026-10-05. A J.D. Power rebuilt-title guide also appeared in search but returned 403, so it was not used.

findings.claim: Gap insurance available through most auto insurers as a policy add-on (typically $20 to $40 per year); dealer gap tends to cost more
findings.correctedValue: III: adding gap to a policy that already has collision and comprehensive costs 'only about $20 a year' on most policies, and most insurers 'typically charge less than the dealer.' The $20-to-$40 range has no primary source (only secondary sites attribute it to III). Suggested: 'Most auto insurers sell gap coverage as an add-on, often for about $20 a year when you already carry collision and comprehensive, according to the Insurance Information Institute, and they typically charge less than a dealership.'
findings.quote: On most auto insurance policies, including gap insurance with collision and comprehensive coverage adds only about $20 a year to the annual premium. ... Your car dealer may offer to sell you gap insurance on your new vehicle. However, most car insurers also offer it, and they typically charge less than the dealer.
findings.sourceName: Insurance Information Institute (Triple-I), 'What is gap insurance?'

findings.claim: According to the Insurance Information Institute, the average collision claim payout has climbed steadily in recent years as vehicle values have risen
findings.correctedValue: III/ISO collision claim severity: 2019 $3,828; 2020 $3,854; 2021 $4,583; 2022 $5,377; 2023 $5,521; 2024 $5,489. It rose every year from 2015 to 2023 and then fell slightly in 2024 (-0.6%), so 'climbed steadily' is not accurate through 2024. The source does not attribute the rise to vehicle values, so drop that causal clause. Suggested: 'According to Insurance Information Institute figures from ISO, the average collision claim rose from $3,828 in 2019 to $5,521 in 2023 before dipping to $5,489 in 2024.'
findings.quote: Private Passenger Auto Insurance Losses, 2015-2024 ... Collision ... 2023: Claim severity $5,521; 2024: Claim severity $5,489. (5) Claim severity is the size of the loss. Source: ISO®, a Verisk Analytics® business.
findings.sourceName: Insurance Information Institute, Facts + Statistics: Auto insurance (ISO/Verisk data)
findings.verified_how: WebFetch of the iii.org page, 2026-10-05. Full collision severity series 2015-2024: 3,377 / 3,454 / 3,517 / 3,665 / 3,828 / 3,854 / 4,583 / 5,377 / 5,521 / 5,489. The quote is a reconstruction of table cells, not running prose.

findings.claim: both the Georgia Office of Insurance and the South Carolina Department of Insurance investigate bad faith valuation practices
findings.correctedValue: Georgia's agency is the 'Office of the Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire' (OCI). Both agencies take consumer complaints about claim handling: GA OCI's Consumer Services Division and SCDOI's Office of Consumer Services, which explicitly covers 'claim disputes'. Neither page uses the words 'investigate bad faith valuation'. Suggested: 'You can file a complaint with the Georgia Office of Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire or the South Carolina Department of Insurance, both of which review consumer complaints about how insurers handle claims.'
findings.quote: GA: 'The Consumer Services Division is the investigative arm of OCI. Our job is to ensure fair and equitable dealings between insurers, agents, and policyholders.' SC: Consumer Services assists with 'coverage issues, claim disputes, premium issues, policy cancellations or non-renewals, refunds, and sales misrepresentations.'
findings.sourceName: Georgia Office of Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire; South Carolina Department of Insurance, Consumer Services
findings.verified_how: WebFetch of oci.georgia.gov and doi.sc.gov/consumers, 2026-10-05. SC complaint filing is at doi.sc.gov/complaint (seen in search results, not fetched).

findings.claim: Check Kelley Blue Book, Edmunds, NADA Guides
findings.correctedValue: NADA Guides is now J.D. Power. J.D. Power bought the NADA Used Car Guide in 2015, and the consumer brand now runs under J.D. Power (jdpower.com/cars). Suggested: 'Kelley Blue Book, Edmunds and J.D. Power (formerly NADA Guides)'.
findings.quote: JD Power Valuation Services, formerly NADA Used Car Guide, has produced its flagship product for 80 years
findings.sourceName: J.D. Power Values (jdpowervalues.com), Official Used Car Guide page
findings.verified_how: WebFetch of jdpowervalues.com, 2026-10-05. J.D. Power press releases on jdpower.com returned 403. The exact rebrand year (secondary sources say 2021) is unverified, so give no date.

findings.claim: Each side hires an independent appraiser, and if the two cannot agree, they select an impartial umpire whose decision is binding. The appraisal process typically costs a few hundred dollars but can recover thousands more than the original offer.
findings.correctedValue: Correct the mechanics: the two appraisers pick the umpire at the start. Each appraiser states the actual cash value and the amount of loss. If they disagree, the differences go to the umpire, and a decision agreed to by any two of the three is binding (the umpire alone does not decide). Each party pays its own appraiser and the two split the appraisal and umpire expenses equally. DROP the cost/recovery sentence: no authoritative source found. Also note that wording varies by insurer and state, so readers should check their own policy. Suggested: 'If you and your insurer disagree on the amount of loss, either side can demand appraisal. Each side picks an appraiser, the two appraisers choose an umpire, and a decision agreed to by any two of the three is binding. You pay your own appraiser and split the umpire's cost with the insurer.'
findings.quote: if the insured and company do not agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal of the loss. In this event, each party will select a licensed appraiser. The two appraisers will select an umpire. The appraisers will state separately the actual cash value and the amount of loss. If they fail to agree, they will submit their differences to the umpire. A decision agreed to by any two will be binding. Each party will 1) Pay its chosen appraiser; and 2) bear the expenses of the appraisal and umpire equally.
findings.sourceName: North Carolina Department of Insurance, 'Common Terms Related to Public Adjusters, Motor Vehicle Damage Appraisers, and Adjusters' (describes the Personal Auto Policy Part D appraisal provision; dated 08.15.22)
findings.verified_how: Downloaded the PDF and extracted its text with pdftotext, 2026-10-05. This is an NC regulator paraphrasing the standard PAP. It is not GA/SC-specific, and the ISO PP 00 01 form text itself was not retrieved. The NC version says 'licensed appraiser' because of NC licensing; the ISO form says 'competent appraiser'. Cost/recovery claim: unverified, drop.

findings.claim: Insurers calculate ACV using comparable sales data pulled from services like CCC Intelligent Solutions or Mitchell; Audatex
findings.correctedValue: All three are total-loss valuation vendors for insurers: CCC Valuation, Mitchell WorkCenter Total Loss, and Audatex (Solera) Autosource. Optionally write 'Audatex (Solera)'.
findings.quote: Mitchell: 'Mitchell WorkCenter Total Loss helps simplify claims by delivering fair-market total loss vehicle valuations...' Solera/Audatex: 'Our extensive vehicle database enables you to receive reliable, regionally adjusted, fair market valuations of total losses.'
findings.verified_how: WebFetch of the Mitchell and Solera pages. CCC confirmed from cccis.com search snippet only ('CCC® Valuation is a leading, automated set of total loss claims settlement services'), not fetched.
